Colormaker Industries Australia is a well-established, family-owned manufacturer of quality coatings for interior and exterior application. Amongst a broad range of technologies, Colormaker also manufactures and exports market leading world class products in textile screen printing inks and high solids epoxy swimming pool coatings. The business is based on Sydney’s Northern Beaches.

We require a dedicated coatings & inks Quality Control (QC) Chemist to join our busy team of specialists in Brookvale, NSW.

Reporting to the Senior Chemist and Technical Manager, the duties and responsibilities of the role will include:

. Performing laboratory tests/QC procedures on paints and raw materials and recommending improvements for Factory Production and Product Development
. Preparing materials for test and/or experimentation
. Performing calculations, computations and measurements
. Analyzing test data results and preparing relevant reviews, reports and summaries
. Auditing and controlling the quality and quantity of materials used in QC tests, R&D and product maintenance
. Checking, calibrating and maintaining test equipment and other laboratory facilities
. Management of Safety Data Sheets, both Raw Materials and Finished Goods
. Technical and other support to Customer Service and Marketing, including translation of technical and other product literature
. Proficient use of Tencia/Arrow, Color I Control and relevant business software (including MS EXCEL). Also use of company systems
. Maintenance of relevant QC and Production records and related administration
. Adhering to appropriate workplace health and safety standards and making recommendations for improvement
. Management of Hazardous Materials and Dangerous Goods.
. Advising and sourcing materials for Research and Development (R&D) projects
. Carrying out product development work on new and existing products

We offer a competitive remuneration package of between $70,000 to $85,000 per annum, excluding superannuation.

The successful candidate will have either:

. A relevant AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma plus five (5) years’ work experience; or
. At least ten (10) years of relevant full-time work experience

The successful candidate must have coatings experience. In particular, high solids epoxy, high performance industrial surface coatings, broad wall architectural and construction membranes etc would be highly regarded, as would knowledge of textile and other screen printing ink technologies. They must also be passionate about the environment, have a good eye for colour and for detail as well as an ability to work with minimal supervision. A high degree of numeracy and literacy in English are mandatory, whilst technical fluency in European languages would be highly regarded.  Applicants must have full and permanent working rights in Australia to be considered.

If you feel that you are suited to the role of Quality Control Chemist, then please send your CV to us via email technical@colormaker.com.au.

Full Time, in Artarmon, New South Wales
Vacancy Listing Dates 2/07/2026 to 30/07/2026
Please Quote Reference Number 17401
- Seeking an Organisation and Methods (Quality Classing) Analyst
- Salary $80,000 + superannuation
- Join Australian Food and Fibre

Australian Food & Fibre (AFF) is a modern, integrated business that combines significant knowledge and expertise to supply quality Australian cotton to the world, as well as cereals, pulses and oil seeds.

We have a career opportunity for a skilled Organisation & Methods (Quality Classing) Analyst to join our team in our Artarmon laboratory, 2064, New South Wales.

Overall Responsibilities:

At the Australian Food & Fibre, Artarmon, facility you are responsible for testing, evaluating and grading our agricultural commodities. They ensure that raw materials (primarily cotton) meet strict domestic and international quality standards before they are exported or sold.

Daily tasks:
- Fibre testing - operating specialised laboratory instruments to analyse the physical properties of cotton samples. This includes measuring fibre length, strength, micronaire (fineness), maturity, and colour.
- Assess current systems - analyse and evaluate capabilities, and workflows to identify bottlenecks and process gaps.
- Commodity grading - applying standardised classing rules to assign grades to cotton lint. This determines the market value and spinning utility of the crop.
- Sample management - preparing, tracking, and cataloguing physical samples sent from various AFF farming and ginning operations (such as their sites in Moree and Narrabri).
- Data Analysis - recording and verifying data within classing and laboratory software systems, ensuring that every batch meets the requirements of export contracts.
- Quality assurance - monitoring laboratory equipment calibration to ensure accurate and reliable test results.
- Classing and compliance - develop, maintain and enforce Quality Auditor standards, reviewing operating procedures and advising on any departures from established guidelines.

Our ideal candidate will have:
- Hands-on trade experience through on-the-job training OR Certificate III in Cotton Ginning OR specialised industry-recognised classing grader advantageous OR an IT background will better equip you with the analytical skills required in our laboratory and for this role.
- Minimum 2+ years of experience in procedural/business/computer analysis, continuous improvement or quality control
- A Bachelor’s degree or higher in Business, IT, Commerce, Operations Management or a related field will be highly regarded.

While a formal agricultural degree can be advantageous for career advancement with us, our hands-on approach for you to function well in the role is to assist you in gaining certification from Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry as part of your induction with us and a requirement for our quality control and cotton exporting criteria.

In return, we can offer:
- Highly competitive salary package ($80,000 + super)
- Excellent professional development and career progression opportunities.
- Supportive, dynamic team environment with hybrid working arrangements.
- Opportunities for ongoing employment and training across seasonal operations.
- Contribution to the local agricultural economy in our regional NSW operations.

Join our company and enjoy a supportive, family-friendly environment where you'll receive in-house assistance and continuous opportunities for up-skilling, ensuring your ongoing professional growth.

result.description:
Power Electronics / Power Systems Engineer
AC Electrical Systems
Motor Control & Starting Systems
Industrial Power Products
Embedded Control Electronics
VFD's, Switchgear, High Current
Long Term Permanent Position

We are looking for a Power Electronics engineer, ideally with practical experience working on AC electrical systems and motors, together with enough design capability to make a meaningful contribution to product development.

If you are in this space, we're keen to hear about:
Where you have worked and what you have worked on
What equipment or products you have worked on
What you have designed and significantly contributed to

The opportunity
Our state-of-the-art design and manufacturing facility in Port Kembla offers a multidisciplinary R&D, engineering and manufacturing environment developing and supporting globally deployed industrial electronic products associated with:
AC motors and motor control
power electronics
soft starters and motor-starting systems
VFDs and motor drives
industrial switching and control
protection, sensing and fault handling
embedded control hardware
current and voltage measurement
released-product improvement and production support
The role can suit a developing or established engineer, but it requires genuine practical experience rather than academic knowledge alone.

What you will work on...
Designing and developing power-electronics circuits and product subsystems.
Contributing to AC-side, mains-side and motor-control product development.
Working with power stages, switching devices, gate drivers, sensing and protection circuits.
Supporting soft starters, VFDs, motor controllers, contactors or related industrial switching products.
Selecting and applying SCRs, TRIACs, MOSFETs, IGBTs or similar switching devices.
Developing or reviewing schematics and PCB designs.
Considering high-current paths, thermal behaviour, EMC, isolation, creepage and clearance.
Building, testing and debugging prototype hardware.
Investigating failures found during development, production testing or field use.
Implementing corrective design changes and validating the results.
Working with embedded firmware, mechanical design, production and product lifecycle engineers.
Producing clear design records, test results and release documentation.
Essential experience
Your experience may be drawn from power electronics, motor control, industrial automation, switchgear, drives, machinery, renewable energy, industrial power conversion or electrical product manufacturing.

You must have:
Professional engineering experience involving AC systems and electric motors.
Substantive design or development capability.
The ability to explain what you personally designed, changed, calculated, selected, programmed, tested or validated.
Experience working with commercial products, electrical or electronic hardware.
An understanding of how designs progress from concept through prototype, test, correction and release.
A relevant qualification in electrical, electronic, power, mechatronics or a related engineering discipline.
Relevant technical experience

Experience in several of the following areas would be valuable:
Three-phase AC motors
induction motors or permanent-magnet motors
motor starting and current limiting
soft starters
variable-frequency drives
motor controllers
inverter power stages
AC-DC or DC-AC conversion
SCR or TRIAC control
MOSFET, IGBT or SiC switching
gate-driver circuits
current and voltage sensing
overcurrent, overvoltage and thermal protection
contactors and industrial switching
power-system or motor-protection interfaces
high-current PCB design
thermal design and component derating
EMC and switching-noise control
galvanic isolation
creepage and clearance
prototype bring-up and fault diagnosis
production and field validation
The design requirement
Applicants must have credible design capability.

This does not necessarily mean that you must have independently architected an entire commercial product. It does mean that you should have made real engineering decisions and be able to explain them.

Examples include:
selecting a circuit or system topology
designing or modifying a power stage
calculating component ratings
selecting switching devices
designing sensing or protection circuits
developing motor-control logic
preparing schematics
reviewing PCB current paths or layout
resolving thermal or EMC problems
changing a design after failed testing
validating a prototype or released-product modification

Candidates whose experience is limited to operating equipment, configuring relays, following test procedures, commissioning systems or reviewing imported designs will need to demonstrate additional personal design contribution / side projects.

Strong backgrounds may include...

We are particularly keen if you have worked for manufacturers, consultancies or engineering teams involved in:
motor drives and VFDs
soft starters
motor-control centres
industrial switchgear
pumps, compressors, fans or rotating equipment
industrial control products
power converters and inverters
UPS or renewable-energy systems
EV charging or electric-drive systems
mining, water, energy or heavy-industry equipment
electrical machinery and industrial automation

What we will ask you about
where you worked
what the company or project produced
what AC system, motor, drive or power product you worked on
the voltage, current and power level where available
what you personally designed
what you configured, integrated, tested or commissioned
which switching devices, controllers or protection systems were involved
whether the work reached prototype, factory test, field validation, production or commercial release
a technical problem you encountered and how you helped resolve it

Apply Now!
Please submit a resume that clearly identifies your relevant design exposure.

Employer questions
Your application will include the following questions:
Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
Do you have experience in a sales role?

Position Overview: Mygration is engaged to source the following position for our client
Our client is a leading innovator in the design, fabrication, and installation of high-quality steel structures and electrical systems for industrial and commercial applications. With a strong focus on engineering excellence, safety, and precision, they deliver cutting-edge solutions across various sectors, including infrastructure, energy, and manufacturing.

We are seeking a skilled Electrical Engineering Technician to join their dynamic team. In this role, you will play a crucial part in supporting the design, installation, and maintenance of electrical systems for heavy machinery, substations, and industrial control systems. You will work closely with engineers and technologists to ensure all electrical installations meet industry standards, safety regulations, and project specifications.

This is an exciting opportunity for a detail-oriented professional with strong technical skills and a passion for electrical systems within an industrial and structural engineering environment.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Design & Documentation:
• Prepare detailed electrical drawings, schematics, and layout plans for industrial installations, including substations, switchgear, motor control systems, and cabling networks.
• Develop wiring diagrams and termination schedules for control panels used in heavy machinery & manufacturing and automation systems.

Technical Support:
• Assist electrical engineers in the design, testing, and optimization of electrical systems for machinery & manufacturing and structural projects.
• Troubleshoot and diagnose faults in PLC-controlled systems, including servo drives and variable frequency drives (VFDs).

Testing & Analysis:
• Conduct electrical tests, perform complex calculations, and analyse data to validate system performance.
• Perform insulation resistance (IR) testing, earth continuity checks, and thermal imaging on high-voltage equipment.

Cost Estimation:
• Assist in estimating material quantities, costs, and project timelines.
• Evaluate supplier quotations for electrical components (e.g., circuit breakers, contactors) to ensure cost-effective procurement.

Quality Assurance:
• Inspect electrical installations and finished products for compliance with specifications.
• Verify that all electrical work adheres to AS/NZS 3000 and IEC standards before commissioning.

Installation & Maintenance:
• Assemble, install, calibrate, and repair electrical equipment, including protection relays and metering devices.
• Perform preventive maintenance on industrial motor control centres (MCCs) to minimize downtime.

Workshop Operations:
• Undertake workshop duties, including wiring, testing, and modifying electrical assemblies.
• Fabricate and test custom control panels for machinery integration.

Research & Development:
• Contribute to R&D initiatives by assisting in experimental programs.
• Assist in the testing and integration of renewable energy systems (e.g., solar inverters) into industrial power networks.

SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS:
• Trade Certification or Diploma in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field.
• Proven experience in electrical drafting, machinery wiring, or industrial electrical systems and manufacturing fabrications.
• Proficiency in CAD software (e.g., AutoCAD Electrical) for schematic and layout design.
• Strong analytical skills with the ability to perform technical calculations and interpret test data.
• Knowledge of industry standards, including AS/NZS 3000 and electrical safety regulations.
• Hands-on experience with motor controls, switchgear, PLCs, and protection systems is highly desirable.
• Workshop & fabrication skills, including the ability to assemble and troubleshoot electrical components.
• Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with engineers and project teams.
• At least 2 years of Full-time on the job work experience.

WHY APPLY?
• Work with a forward-thinking company at the forefront of industrial and structural engineering.
• Engage in high-impact projects involving cutting-edge electrical systems.
• Opportunities for professional growth and skill development.
• Competitive remuneration and a supportive team environment.

If you are a motivated Electrical Engineering Technician with a passion for precision and innovation, we encourage you to apply! Submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your relevant experience.

Please note: We are recruiting on behalf of our client. All applications will be treated with confidentiality.

result.description:
Motor Mechanic 
Davey Automotive Services – Breakwater, VIC, 3219
Permanent, full-time | $79,423 plus superannuation 

About us

Davey Automotive Services is a professional automotive workshop based in Breakwater, providing mechanical repairs, servicing and vehicle support for private, commercial and fleet customers.

The business specialises in scheduled servicing, diagnostics, mechanical repairs, vehicle inspections, roadworthy requirements, parts support and after-sales care. With experience across all makes and models, Davey Automotive Services delivers practical, reliable and detail-focused automotive services tailored to our customer’s needs.

The workshop is operated with a strong focus on workmanship, safety and customer confidence. Each vehicle is assessed and prepared with care to ensure it meets expected standards of performance, reliability and roadworthiness.

The role 

We are seeking a qualified and experienced Motor Mechanic to join our team. The role involves maintaining, testing, diagnosing and repairing petrol engines and the mechanical parts of lightweight motor vehicles, including transmissions, suspension, steering and braking systems.

You will be responsible for carrying out scheduled servicing, fault diagnosis, repairs, parts replacement and performance testing in accordance with manufacturer specifications, service manuals and workshop procedures. The role requires accurate diagnosis of mechanical and electrical faults, safe dismantling and reassembly of vehicle components, and the use of appropriate hand tools, workshop equipment and computer-based diagnostic systems.

The successful candidate will be expected to work efficiently within a busy workshop, maintain accurate records of work completed, support the preparation and ongoing servicing of vehicles, and ensure all work is completed safely and to the required standard.

Flexibility is essential, as the role may involve working across business operating hours, including Saturdays.

Key duties and responsibilities 

- Maintain, test and repair petrol engines and mechanical components of lightweight motor vehicles.
- Detect and diagnose mechanical and electrical faults in engines, transmissions, suspension, steering, braking systems and related vehicle components.
- Use computer-based diagnostic equipment, testing procedures and road testing where required to identify faults and confirm repair outcomes.
- Dismantle and remove engine assemblies, transmissions, steering mechanisms and other components, and inspect parts for wear, damage or defects.
- Repair, adjust or replace worn, damaged or defective parts and reassemble mechanical components with reference to service manuals and manufacturer specifications.
- Perform scheduled maintenance services, including oil changes, lubrication, filter replacement, safety checks and engine tune-ups, to support smooth vehicle operation and compliance with pollution requirements.
- Reassemble engines and mechanical parts after repairs have been completed.
- Test and adjust repaired mechanical parts and systems to ensure proper performance, roadworthiness and safe operation. 
- Inspect vehicles and identify work required to achieve roadworthiness, where required and where permitted by applicable regulatory requirements.
- Maintain accurate records of inspections, servicing, repairs, parts used and work completed.
- Maintain a clean, organised and safe workshop and ensure compliance with workplace health and safety requirements at all times.

Required qualifications and experience 

- Certificate III in automotive mechanical technology at least two (2) years of relevant experience; or
- Certificate IV or higher in automotive mechanical technology and at least one (1) year of relevant experience; or
- At least three (3) years of highly relevant work experience may substitute for the above formal qualifications.

How to apply 

We welcome applications from all appropriately qualified candidates. We are committed to a fair, inclusive recruitment process, and we will consider applicants based on skills, experience and role requirements.

Please submit your application through the recruitment platform for this advertisement.
Your application should include:

- A current resume outlining your relevant qualifications and work experience; and 
- A brief cover letter addressing your suitability for the role. 

To ensure all applications are properly received and assessed, please submit your application via one platform only and do not to apply through multiple job portals.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Engineering Technologist (protection) - Full Time
$80,000-85,000 AUD annually plus superannuation
A.C.N. 656 274 501 PTY LTD T/A Spark Professional Services
Stimson St, Guildford, NSW 2161
ABN 40 656 274 501
About Us:
Spark Professional Services is a leading Australian provider of high and low-voltage electrical engineering solutions, delivering specialised services in testing, commissioning, protection systems, switching, maintenance, and engineering design. With over 15 years of industry expertise, the company supports critical infrastructure projects across data centres, mining, renewable energy, utilities, commercial and industrial facilities, and transport infrastructure sectors.
The successful candidate will contribute to the delivery of protection engineering projects including data centre switchgear systems, substations, transmission and distribution networks, and industrial power infrastructure.
Duties and Responsibilities:
1.	Analyse and interpret existing and emerging engineering technologies related to protection philosophies, single-line diagrams, and relay schematics for power system protection. 
2.	Apply technological advancements in the design, configuration, and application of protection relays and schemes. 
3.	Assist engineers in designing and developing protection schemes for electrical systems, including transformers, feeders and generators. 
4.	Configure, program, and set protection relays in accordance with coordination studies. 
5.	Perform protection coordination and grading studies to ensure selectivity and reliability of the protection system. 
6.	Troubleshoot and diagnose protection relay malfunctions, mis-operations, and scheme design issues. 
7.	Recommend modifications and improvements to protection schemes based on technical evaluations and fault analysis. 
8.	Review relay settings and protection schemes for compliance with utility, regulatory, and industry standards. 
9.	Assist in the commissioning and functional testing of protection schemes, ensuring correct relay operation and system integration. 
10.	Collaborate with testing and commissioning technologists, engineers, and technicians to integrate new protection technologies into ongoing projects. 
11.	Identify and investigate protection system failures, trips, and abnormalities, recommending corrective actions. 
12.	Perform periodic reviews and updates of protection settings to reflect system changes and load growth across client networks. 
13.	Ensure protection system designs comply with regulatory requirements, grid codes, and industry standards. 
14.	Monitor and enforce safety measures related to protection system design, settings changes, and implementation. 
15.	Prepare technical reports, protection setting sheets, coordination studies, and documentation for projects and system modifications. 
16.	Maintain accurate records of relay settings, coordination studies, protection scheme changes, and test results. 
Required Skills, Qualifications & Experience
•	Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering Technology, Electrical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline
•	Minimum 1 year of relevant industry experience in protection systems, testing, commissioning, or electrical infrastructure projects
•	Knowledge of HV/MV protection systems, protection relay testing, and commissioning practices
•	Familiarity with protection coordination, SCADA integration, and fault diagnosis within electrical networks
•	Experience using engineering and protection software such as ETAP, DigSILENT PowerFactory, or similar systems
•	Understanding of AS/NZS standards, WHS legislation, and electrical safety procedures
•	Strong analytical, technical troubleshooting, and documentation skills
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within project teams
•	Willingness to travel to project sites as required
•	What We Offer
•	Competitive salary package and superannuation
•	Professional development and career progression opportunities
•	Exposure to major infrastructure and electrical engineering projects
•	Supportive and technically focused working environment
